subject: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex

Hi Ana —

Thanks again for the useful discussion today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the trial: 

Call recap / goals:
- Scope: 3-week POC to validate Redwood inference for Globex's multi-lingual customer support assistant.
- Primary languages: English + Spanish; secondary: French for select flows.
- Key success criteria discussed: response accuracy on knowledge-base Q&A (>85% automated answer rate), hallucination rate <3% on sampled prompts, latency (p95) <300ms for short queries, and total token cost under $X per 1k tokens target (we'll baseline this during week 1).

Proposed POC plan (high level):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange evaluation prompts + sample KB exports; complete basic security questionnaire.
- Week 1: baseline tests (latency, cost) with recommended open model; quick feedback loop on prompt engineering.
- Week 2: focused quality evals across English/Spanish/French; run regression checks and fallback scenarios.
- Week 3: final report, rollout recommendations, and next-step commercial proposal.

Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary: Llama 2 13B-chat (quantized int8 where applicable) — good balance of accuracy, latency, multilingual coverage, and cost.
- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct (lower-cost variant) used for burst/availability fallback and constrained-latency routes.
- We will also evaluate a larger Llama-2-70B-chat variant in a small subset of tests if you want to see quality delta for hard cases.

Ownership / roles:
- Sales lead: me (Ben) — contract, logistics, scheduling.
- Technical lead: Marissa — model config, prompts, eval harness.
- CS/Success: Laura — adoption criteria and rollout readiness.

Next steps requested from Globex:
1) Share an initial set of 50-100 evaluation prompts across English/Spanish/French (mix of KB lookup and open-ended support).
2) Confirm data residency / SOC2 requirements (I attached the SOC2 stub we reference).
3) Kickoff availability — we're proposing Tue, Jun 22 for a 60-minute kickoff and environment handover.

Attachments: POC-plan-Globex-v1.pdf (high-level plan), SOC2_Audit_Report_stub.pdf

I'll follow up with Marissa for the technical runbook after we get the prompt set.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the ask from our side:
- We'll send a starter set of 75 prompts (50 EN, 15 ES, 10 FR) by EOD Wed.
- SOC2 is a hard requirement for production; for the POC we can proceed with the stub but will need the full SOC2 evidence before any Dedicated deployment.
- Data residency: all customer data must remain in the US for this workload.

A couple of follow-ups re: models: 
- We care about Spanish performance especially for multi-turn context; does Llama 2 13B-chat handle ES multi-turn well, or should we start with a larger variant?
- For fallback: we need clear rules if the fallback model has a different hallucination profile — is Redwood able to route back to primary for critical queries?

We'll review the POC-plan and approve scheduling for Jun 22 once we receive the kickoff invite.

Thanks,
Ana Gomez
Head of Product, AI Assistants | Globex Corp
ana.gomez@globex.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Ana Gomez <ana.gomez@globex.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex

Hi Ana / Ben —

Quick technical note on model selection and the evaluation plan: 

Model tradeoffs:
- Llama 2 13B-chat (quantized int8): recommended as primary for the POC — best balance of latency and token cost while retaining decent multi-lingual performance. In our internal benchmarks Llama 2 13B-chat achieves strong ES/EN parity on retrieval-augmented queries when prompts are tuned.
- If you want stronger ES multi-turn quality out of the gate, we can include Llama 2 70B-chat as a quality control arm for a small subset (~5% of queries) to measure delta.
- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct (quantized) — lower cost and faster cold-starts. Redwood routing policies can be configured so:
  * normal routing -> primary (13B)
  * if latency SLO violated or primary capacity saturated -> fallback (7B)
  * critical queries (tagged by your app) -> preferentially route to primary or to an isolated dedicated pool.
  * We can also implement a verification step: run critical responses through a lightweight reranker or hallucination-checker before returning to user (adds small latency).

Evaluation plan / metrics (we will own the harness):
- Accuracy (KB retrieval + answer correctness) — human-labeled sample (goal: >85% automated answer coverage).
- Hallucination rate — human-eval on sample (goal: <3%).
- Latency — p95 target <300ms (short queries), p50 <120ms.
- Cost — tokens-per-response baseline and projected cost per 1k tokens; we will provide a weekly cost dashboard.
- Multilingual checks — per-language F1 and human-satisfaction score on Spanish/French subsets.

Ownership & instrumentation:
- We'll set up an evaluation Drive folder and a small HubSpot playbook to track prompts and results.
- Marissa (me) will own the eval harness and weekly reports.
- Laura will compile adoption criteria and success signoff.

I'll attach a short runbook and sample eval template (in the POC-plan PDF). If Globex can share the prompt set and a small sample KB export (CSV), we can begin baseline tests immediately.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. A couple of operational constraints from security and product: 
- We'll need confirmation that the POC environment will be isolated to US regions and that any logs containing PII can be redacted or excluded from retention.
- For the evaluation dataset: we'll provide the prompts and a small KB CSV (sample 500 rows) by Thu. Please include Spanish and French testers in the human-eval pool.
- For fallback behavior: we want the option to always route 'billing' and 'legal' categories to primary model — can you add category-based routing to the configuration?

If you can confirm those items and send a calendar invite for Jun 22 kickoff, we'll be good to go.

Best,
Ana
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & evaluation plan for Globex

Ana —

Great — confirming the following items and next steps: 
1) Redwood will provision a US-only POC environment and provide controls to redact/exclude PII from logs for the POC. Full SOC2 evidence will be provided upon request; we included a stub in the attachments.
2) We'll add category-based routing so 'billing' and 'legal' are forced to the primary model; Marissa will implement as a rule in the routing policy.
3) Please send prompts + KB CSV by end of day Thu (thanks in advance).
4) Kickoff: Tue, Jun 22 at 10:00 AM PT — invite sent (includes Zoom + Drive folder + HubSpot link).

Deliverables before kickoff:
- Redwood: preconfigured evaluation harness, baseline runs on Llama 2 13B-chat and Mistral 7B Instruct, and a short demo of routing policies.
- Globex: prompt set, KB CSV, and list of categories to tag as critical.

I'll also attach the DocuSign link for the POC engagement (simple MSA + trial addendum). Signing will let us turn on dedicated routing and SLO monitoring for the trial.

Look forward to the kickoff — thanks everyone for the quick turn.

Best,
Ben
